lesson_title: Naming Triangles by Sides and Angles
hook_text: Can a triangle be right-angled AND equilateral? Never. Here is why.
clip_script: An equilateral triangle is always acute-angled, because every angle is sixty degrees. So right-angled equilateral and obtuse-angled equilateral are impossible combinations. A right-angled isosceles triangle has a ninety-degree angle and two equal sides. Its other two angles are equal and add to ninety, so each is forty-five degrees.
visual_style: A roof truss with triangles highlighted one by one; side dashes and corner arcs appear; a set square slides in labelled right-angled isosceles.
pacing: Question hook, quick proof, set-square example.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to name any triangle by sides and angles.
